newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank says injecting funds on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank says injecting funds on Friday.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank, reacting as money rates bubbled ever higher, said it would inject funds into the banking system on Friday and keep a close eye on liquidity flows in the banking system.

A central bank official said the bank would execute open market operations on Friday through bills finance companies, using qualified securities instruments offered by interested financial institutions.
"The central bank will continue to keep a close watch on the liquidity flow of banks," the offical told Reuters.
Taiwan's overnight interbank rate closed higher for the ninth consecutive session on Thursday to reach a 21-month peak of 8.957 percent and rocketed into double digits on Friday.
The rate stood at 10.461 percent at mid-session on Friday.
The central bank said interested financial institutions should contact the bank directly.
Bids would close at 1130 a.m. (0330 GMT).
Funds would be released according to actual demand, the central bank said.
